correctness.rationale: For matching unanimous graph, ordered 2-blocks reversed in order preserve every unanimous preference twice and orient all other pairs once in each direction. An arbitrary triple contains two unanimous edges with exact probability 6*3^(-n)-6*6^(-n), by six extreme events with complete-order overlap, so the union bound yields high-probability solvability. For unanimous-edge count X, disjoint candidate-pair orientation sigma-fields are independent, joint incident edge probability is 2*3^(-n)+2*6^(-n); explicit Arratia-Goldstein-Gordon neighborhood bound tends to zero when m/2^(n/2)->c, yielding Poisson(c²). The standalone checker exhaustively compares 14,652 ranking input profiles plus probability identities. Asymptotic claims are proved analytically, not inferred from tests.

value.rationale: The motivating paper explicitly asks for probability-model existence results after proving adversarial impossibility. The theorem supplies a constructive answer for an exponentially growing number of alternatives, plus a sharp nontrivial Poisson transition for the natural simplest mirror algorithm that a block method overcomes. This characterizes a meaningful structural mechanism (sparse unanimity graph), not an arbitrary small numerical statistic. Scope is restricted to impartial culture and two outputs, with no unsupported claim of an overall sharp representability threshold.
